text: The per-service login of rwb-agent under DP-02 is not named by any source. The three stories name it 'the rwb-agent login (DP-02)' and the chart references it through a platform secret, never a literal.
why: DP-02 requires one login per service and the legacy story names only the agent identity SY-AGENT and the roles.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 10; context pack P10 (one login per service, DP-02); Template and Rules v1 R4.
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP sections 3 and 10; RWB-P10-E2028-CON sections 3 and 10; RWB-P10-E2028-OPS sections 3, 10 and 12.7
confirm: Platform administrator with the ACE database team at the wave 2 release review
impact: A wrong name fails the migration job and every grant check; no business behaviour changes.

text: The decision code 'D6' of a feedback is the assumed LOV-DECISION code the legacy story names. It is read as the value of the approved policy row and reference data and is never written in the source.
why: Legacy BR3 marks D6 as an assumed code; no source publishes the LOV-DECISION list.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 8 BR3; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.2; context pack P10 (reference data through rwb-case).
confirm: Owner of rwb-case reference data and RW-COE at the contract freeze
impact: The record of every verdict carries the code; a list change is a data change, not a release.

text: The business date against which agent_run.data_as_of is compared for the stale warning of AC9 is the business date answered by the rwb-source-data freshness read (GET /freshness of Arch v5 slide 15); when the read fails, the summary is shown with the stale warning and no current date is claimed.
why: The freshness rule of the FSD names v_ace_batch_status, which rwb-agent may not read, and no other operation of this key answers a business date.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 5 and 7 AC9; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.7.3.1 VR-P10-007-1; context pack P10 (ACE data only through the owner's contract).
confirm: Owner of rwb-source-data at the contract freeze
impact: Decides which dates raise MSG-P1-001; a wrong date either hides a stale summary or warns falsely.

text: The acceptance event of an L1 verdict is named rwb.agent.AgentFeedbackRecorded.v1 on rwb.agent.events.v1 under the naming rule of R4, because the catalogue names only AgentRunCompleted (EV-28) for the agent topic. The record of the verdict is the library type DecisionRecorded on rwb.decision-record.v1 and is a separate message.
why: The catalogue holds one event of the agent topic and DP-03 names the shared record topic but not its type name.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 12; context pack P10 (EV-28, topic and event naming, shared record topic); Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-03 and DP-09.
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP section 12.3; RWB-P10-E2028-CON sections 7 AC6, 12.3 and 18
confirm: Platform event owner and the data steward at the contract freeze
impact: Fixes the registry subject, the consumer groups and the acceptance count of the monitor.

text: The seven list codes (LOV-PRODUCT, LOV-REGION, LOV-AUTONOMY, LOV-FEEDBACK, LOV-DECISION, LOV-AGENT, LOV-AGENT-RUN) are service configuration of rwb-agent and their values are reference data of rwb-case, read through its reference-data contract before an answer is served or a verdict stored.
why: The legacy story names the lists but no source says which service owns their values, and DP-07 makes reference data rwb-case's.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 8 and 11; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.2; context pack P10 (DP-07).
confirm: Owner of rwb-case reference data at the contract freeze
impact: A list change is a data change of its owner and never a release of rwb-agent.

text: The case-decision proposal operation of rwb-case has no published path. The stories name the operation, build against the rwb-case fake and take the path from RWB-P3-E1035-CON when it is published; no caller invents a path of its own.
why: The legacy monolith proposed the verdict in process and no contract document of this run publishes the path.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 4 and 12; context pack P10 (the case is P3's; one hop and 2 s).
confirm: Owner of rwb-case at the contract freeze
impact: Blocks only the case-record proposal, not the verdict, the record or the panel.

text: The gateway-bff route in front of the two operations has no published path or name. The stories declare one pass-through route of one hop that preserves the query, the If-Match header, the media type and the refusals, and take the path from the edge contract of RWB-PLT-N001-CON when it is published.
why: DP-19 requires the route and no source names it; a screen must never reach the service.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 4; context pack P10 (gateway-bff, one hop, 2 s; DP-19).
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP sections 12.8 and 15; RWB-P10-E2028-CON sections 7 AC7, 13 and 15; RWB-P10-E2028-OPS sections 7 AC9, 13 and 15
confirm: Edge team at the contract freeze
impact: Unreachable panel if the route and the registration disagree; no data change.

text: The member names of the answer, of the request and of the eligibility answer are fixed by the contract of this key; their physical types and the maximum lengths of summary and gapType beyond the table lengths of the TSD are left to the review with the owners, and the form of recordedAt and dataAsOf is a date or timestamp as the platform problem and payload conventions require.
why: The legacy story gives member names and three lengths; no source gives REST types.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 11 and 12; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (item_key varchar(20), verdict varchar(10), reason varchar(1000)).
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the solution architect at the contract freeze
impact: A type change after the baseline is a breaking change with a new version.

text: The 409 of the feedback operation is settled by the unique key of agent_run_id and item_key first and by the If-Match row version second, and both carry MSG-GEN-004 and leave one record and one feedback row.
why: The legacy operation carries both checks with one message and no source states the order.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 5 X4, 8 BR5 and 12; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent at the contract freeze
impact: Decides which check answers a repeat; one verdict per run and item either way.

text: The legacy feature flag rwb.agent.intake-l1 is held as a data row of the platform feature-flag library (the default ruling of R3). Off, the agent-outputs read answers an empty list and the panel is hidden; in the environments it is off in DEV and on in SIT and UAT only after the smoke read answers.
why: The monolith property file has no counterpart and R3 gives feature flags to the platform library.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 13 (feature flag); Template and Rules v1 R3 default ruling.
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP sections 5 X12 and 13; RWB-P10-E2028-OPS sections 4 and 7 AC6
confirm: Platform library owner at the release review
impact: The switch is the only way to withdraw the panel without a release.

text: The topics rwb.agent.events.v1 and rwb.decision-record.v1 are provisioned with a retry topic and a .dlt topic under the platform convention, and their partition count, replication factor and retention are environment values of the release, not values of this WP.
why: DP-09 fixes the retry and .dlt rule and no source fixes the topic sizing.
read: Context pack P10 (Kafka with outbox and inbox, CloudEvents, retry and .dlt per service; DP-09); Template and Rules v1 R4.
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP sections 12.3 and 18; RWB-P10-E2028-OPS sections 4, 12.3 and 18
confirm: Platform event owner at the release review
impact: A missing .dlt topic loses refused messages; sizing changes throughput only.

text: The migration of agent_feedback keeps the legacy file name V10_008__agent_feedback.sql and applies in the rwb-agent Flyway sequence of schema rwb_agent after the earlier P10 migrations of the service; no source lists the P10 migration sequence, so the order is decided by the sequence and never by a release of another service.
why: The legacy story fixes the file name and no source fixes its place in the order.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 section 13; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-15; context pack P10 (per-service Flyway).
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP sections 13 and 18; RWB-P10-E2028-OPS sections 13 and 18
confirm: ACE database team with the DevOps team at the release review
impact: A wrong order blocks the rollout; the forward-only rule keeps the table after a rollback.

text: Replica counts, resource sizes, probe paths and timings, the worker build ID and version set, the KEDA minimum and maximum, the activity and outbox timeouts, the topology, the host, the SKU and the budget, the alert windows and the floors and ceilings of the acceptance and override series, and the dashboard series retention are environment values: the chart exposes them by name and no value is hard-coded or written into this WP.
why: No source carries a deployment number, and the legacy story has no chart, no queue and no alert rule.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 3, 4 and 13; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T7; context pack P10 (queue rwb-agent, namespace rwb-recovery, observability).
confirm: DevOps team with the platform administrator at the release review
impact: Decides when an alert fires and how the worker scales; no business value changes.

text: The consumer groups of rwb.agent.events.v1 belong to the services that consume the topic (rwb-decision, rwb-document, rwb-deviation and rwb-reporting) and are created by their own releases. The rwb-agent release verifies that each consume right exists and creates none of them.
why: One service may not create another service's group, and the legacy story names no group.
read: Context pack P10 (Kafka with outbox and inbox; one topic per service); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-09.
confirm: Platform event owner with the four consumer services at the release review
impact: A group created in the wrong release breaks the ownership of the feed lag.

text: The item key set of an intake output is the single item SUMMARY, as the legacy story fixes it; a second item key is outside the contract of this version.
why: No source lists item keys and the legacy BR5 fixes SUMMARY.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent at the contract freeze
impact: A second item needs a new contract version.

text: A verdict outside LOV-FEEDBACK, a missing item key or a request member outside its list is refused with 422 and the platform message MSG-GEN-001 naming the member, and nothing is read or written.
why: The legacy operation gives 422 for a missing reason with MSG-P7-005 only and states no message for an invalid member.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 5 X2 and 12; FSD P10 Agent runtime v3 A2.6.3.1 VR-P10-006-1 (MSG-GEN-001).
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-agent with the platform owner of the message catalogue
impact: Decides the message an invalid verdict shows; no record and no feedback row is written.

text: The mode, the segment product group and region, the segment threshold, the confidence floor and the model timeout the L1 gate reads are columns of the approved agent_policy row of schema rwb_agent, loaded and approved through the operations of RWB-P10-E1061-CON. This story reads them as a version and writes none of them.
why: The legacy loader table has no counterpart, and no source in this key says how policy version P2 is loaded.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-028 sections 3 and 8 BR1; TSD P10 Agent runtime v2 T3.1 (DF-AGT-008 to DF-AGT-012, DF-AGT-021 to DF-AGT-023); context pack P10 (own schema, DP-01).
applied_in: RWB-P10-E2028-APP sections 2, 3 BR8 and 13; RWB-P10-E2028-CON sections 7 AC4 and 18
confirm: Owner of rwb-agent with RW-RISK at the wave 2 contract freeze
impact: Fixes the L1 gate as data; a policy row is a data change and the story writes none of it.
